summary: Full Riftbound test pass: headless tracer invariants + monkey gameplay-flow + per-card playtest on N untested cards. Returns one merged report.
logs: [lane13 (2 cards)] failed: API Error: 529 Overloaded. This is a server-side issue, usually temporary — try again in a moment. If it persists, check https://status.claude.com.

findings.what: Step 28 was a harness click timeout; engine state, moves, energy (0) and resource bar ('Energy 0 Runes 3/4') are identical to step 27 and consistent, no pendingChoice, Recruit token correctly shown exhausted/rotated. The only rules-facing oddity visible: every card in player-1's hand (Retreat, Garbage Grabber, Vanguard Captain, Noxian Emissary, Mushroom Pouch) carries a prominent 'HIDE' button even though none has the [Hidden] keyword and the engine offers no hideCard move for them.
findings.why_wrong: 'Hide' is a defined game action reserved for cards with the Hidden keyword (rule 8xx Hidden: 'Hide now for [rainbow] to react with later') — and a real Hidden card (Windsinger) is in this very game. Labeling a client-only cosmetic toggle 'HIDE' on non-Hidden cards misrepresents a rules action to the player; it should use a non-rules term (e.g. 'Conceal'/'eye icon') or only appear where the Hide action is legal.
findings.ruleOrCard: Hidden keyword / Hide action (rule 129.4, 8xx Hidden); apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/render/card.js W13 toggle
findings.reason: card.js:195-204 (W13) sets hideBtn = `<button class="card-hide-btn" ...>Hide</button>` whenever `zone === "hand" && isOwned && card.id` — no check for the Hidden keyword or for an available hideCard move — and it is emitted on every hand card at line 247. Rule 811.1/811.1.c defines "Hide" as the Discretionary Action whose prerequisite is the Hidden keyword, and the engine implements a real `hideCard` move (moves/play/hide.ts, registered in moves/cards.ts:29). So a client-only localStorage cosmetic toggle is labeled with the rules term "Hide" on non-Hidden cards, exactly as claimed.

findings.what: Playing Facebreaker via Hidden reveal (revealHidden) gives no target choice; engine auto-picks the friendly and enemy unit.
findings.expected: "Stun a friendly unit and an enemy unit at the same battlefield" — when revealed from facedown with 2 friendly + 2 enemy units at that battlefield, the player should be prompted to choose which friendly and which enemy unit to stun (as playSpell from hand does via per-target move params).
findings.observed: revealHidden move only takes {cardId, playerId}; chain item was created with no `targets` and no pendingChoice; on resolution the engine stunned token-recruit-player-1-13 and token-recruit-player-2-15 (first of each) while -14 and -16 stayed unstunned. No prompt at any point.
findings.reason: Reproduced and traced. hide.ts:605-720 — revealHidden params are only {playerId, cardId, paidAdditionalCost?} (types/moves.ts:253); enumerator pushes no target variants; reducer (hide.ts:768-785) adds the spell chain item with no `targets`. At resolution, resolve.ts:392-397 lifts a prompt target via findSequenceLeadTarget, but targeting.ts:113-125 returns undefined for Facebreaker's two distinct slots (friendly@battlefield + enemy@same), so the choose-target pendingChoice branch (resolve.ts:517-530) is never reached. The sequence handler then auto-picks: sequence.ts:215-238 picks the lead via `candidates.find(...) ?? candidates[0]` and sequence.ts:198-202 picks the "same" unit via `pool.slice(0,1)`. Repro harness test (2 friendly + 2 enemy at bf1, hide→advanceTurn→reveal→both pass): reveal option had fields:[], chain item had no targets, no pick decision surfaced, and h1/a1 were stunned while h2/a2 were not. By contrast playSpell (play-spell.ts:830-856) enumerates per-pair `targets` variants for the same card.

findings.what: Play-cost modal mislabels multi-unit sacrifice variants for Commander Ledros
findings.expected: Each play variant button should name the units being killed as the additional cost (e.g. 'Play + sacrifice Marai + Poro') so the player can tell the options apart; Ledros has no Accelerate
findings.observed: Every variant with sacrificeIds.length>=2 renders as 'Play + Accelerate — 6 + additional cost — enters ready' (4 identical buttons at order=2 with 3 friendly units); describePlayVariant in public/js/gameplay/render/modals.js only handles single sacrificeId and falls through to the Accelerate label. Clicking one still executes the correct multi-kill move and Ledros enters exhausted.
findings.reason: modals.js:147-161 — describePlayVariant only branches on m.params.sacrificeId (singular); any paidAdditionalCost variant without it falls through to `label: 'Play + Accelerate', detail: '${baseCost} + ${extra} — enters ready'` where extra defaults to 'additional cost' when no additionalCostSpec. The engine enumerator at play-unit.ts:693-702 emits Ledros kill-any-number variants with `sacrificeIds: subset` and only adds `sacrificeId` when subset.length === 1, so every multi-unit subset (4 of them with 3 killable units: 3 pairs + 1 triple) renders identically as 'Play + Accelerate — 6 + additional cost — enters ready'.

findings.what: Conditional Shield 3 static ability is not implemented — the parser emits the second ability as {type:'static', effect:{type:'raw', text:'I have [Shield 3] while I'm at a battlefield with exactly one other unit you control.'}} and the engine ignores 'raw' statics.
findings.expected: With Disciple of Shen (1 might) + exactly one other friendly unit (1 might) defending a P1-controlled battlefield against a 4-might attacker, Disciple should have Shield 3 (keywords include Shield, defends as 4) so defenders total 5 and the attacker dies.
findings.observed: game.state(disciple).keywords == ['Hidden'] only (no Shield) both alone and with exactly one other friendly unit; in the engine-harness combat probe both defenders went to trash and the 4-might attacker conquered bf1 (defenders counted 1+1=2). Live client state also exposes no Shield grant.
findings.reason: Ran the real card registry (getCardRegistry() from packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/all-cards.ts) for ven-117-166: enrichCards re-parses rulesText and yields abilities = [{keyword:'Hidden',type:'keyword'}, {type:'static', effect:{type:'raw', text:"I have [Shield 3] while I'm at a battlefield with exactly one other unit you control."}}] — no condition, no grant-keyword. In the engine, recalculateStaticEffects (packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/static-abilities.ts:715-743) only admits effect types in PASS_1_EFFECTS {grant-keyword, grant-keywords} and PASS_2_EFFECTS {modify-might}; a 'raw' effect is filtered out at lines 737-743 (`passEffects.length === 0 -> continue`), so no Shield keyword is ever granted. No card-specific override exists (JSON_CARD_ENGINE_FLAGS at all-cards.ts:802-822 has no ven-117-166 entry; grep for ven-117/Disciple in engine and app finds nothing). Hence Disciple of Shen never gets Shield 3 and defends at 1 might, matching the observed behavior.

findings.what: Board card 'Effective Might' badge ignores meta.extraBuffs, so Lee Sin's 'any number of buffs' stacking is not reflected in the UI.
findings.expected: After a second [Exhaust]: Buff me resolves (meta.buffed=true, meta.extraBuffs=1), the board might badge should read 7 (5 base + 2 buffs), matching the engine (engine test 'second activation stacks a second buff (7 might)' passes).
findings.observed: public/js/gameplay/render/card.js computes effMight with `(card.meta?.buffed ? 1 : 0)` only; the .card-might badge showed '6' after both the first and the second buff even though state meta was {buffed:true, extraBuffs:1}. (combat.js showdown renderer ignores buffs entirely: base+mightModifier+staticMightBonus.)
findings.reason: apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/render/card.js:219-220 computes effMight = baseMight + mightModifier + staticMightBonus + (meta.buffed ? 1 : 0) + equipmentMightBonus + combatRoleMightBonus, with no extraBuffs term; grep for "extraBuffs" across public/js returns nothing. Engine consistently adds (meta.extraBuffs ?? 0) (e.g. abilities/effects/_helpers.ts:85, target-resolver.ts:774, effects/buff.ts:45 increments extraBuffs on stacked buff). server/snapshot.ts:396 spreads full baseMeta so extraBuffs reaches the client, but the badge ignores it -> shows 6 instead of 7 for Lee Sin's second buff.

findings.what: After Evelynn's play-from-hidden trigger moved an enemy Mech from the other battlefield to Evelynn's battlefield (controlled by me, not contested), no Contested status was applied and no combat was staged; the board sat in Neutral Open with opposing units co-located and the engine instead offered me (the controller) a manual 'contestBattlefield'/'startShowdown' move.
findings.expected: Per rules 190/323.11.a the arriving enemy unit's controller applies Contested to my battlefield, a Combat is staged (323.9) and begins (323.13) with player-2 attacking and Evelynn/Phantom defending. Engine's stageCombatOnArrival (abilities/effects/move.ts) returns early unless bf.contested is already true, so effect-driven moves into an uncontested controlled battlefield never stage combat.
findings.observed: battlefields[bf].contested=false, controller=player-1, interaction.showdown=null, all unit combatRole=null; Mech(player-2), Phantom, Evelynn all idle at same battlefield; availableMoves = endTurn/standardMove/contestBattlefield.
findings.reason: Evelynn (unl-141-219) uses `{type:"move", to:"here", target:{controller:"enemy",type:"unit"}}`. In handle_move the `dest === "here"` branch (move.ts:574-597) calls moveCardWithEvent for each target then stageCombatOnArrival(ctx, targetZone) — but never markContestedOnArrival. stageCombatOnArrival (move.ts:53-62) derives attackingPlayer only when `bf.contested === true` and returns early otherwise, so an enemy unit dragged into an uncontested battlefield controlled by Evelynn's player never gets Contested applied and no combat roles/showdown are staged. Contrast the other effect-move branches which do call markContestedOnArrival (move.ts:252/254 swap, :326 chosen-battlefield, :488 BattlefieldLocation) and pending-choice.ts:1379 (choose-destination → contestBattlefieldOnArrival). The state-based-check fallback (cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:882 pushes bfId to combatPending when 2+ owners share an uncontested bf) is never consumed outside tests, so nothing else repairs the state. Result matches observation: contested=false, no combatRole, manual contestBattlefield offered.

findings.what: Petricite Monument (plain Gear, no [Equip]/Equipment subtype) is offered an `equipCard` move and the engine accepts it, attaching the Monument to a friendly unit for free.
findings.expected: Only Equipment gear can be attached to units; a non-Equipment gear like Petricite Monument should have no equipCard move and the move should be rejected.
findings.observed: moves list contained equipCard {equipmentId: ...sfd-104-221, unitId: Flame Chompers}; executing it returned success and state showed Monument meta.attachedTo=<unit>, unit meta.equippedWith=[Monument], no cost paid.
findings.reason: equipCard enumerator (equipment.ts:92-96) and condition (equipment.ts:145) gate only on `cardType === "equipment" || cardType === "gear"` — no Equipment subtype/tag/Equip-keyword check. Petricite Monument (riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/petricite-monument.ts) is `cardType: "gear"` with no Equip, so it passes both filters; reducer (196-218) then sets attachedTo/equippedWith with no cost charged (comment at line 61 admits Equip cost not charged). Bug reproduced by code inspection.

findings.what: History log narrates playGear as an equip.
findings.expected: "dev played Petricite Monument." (it is a gear played to base, not equipment attached to a unit)
findings.observed: Log entry: "dev equipped Petricite Monument." (server/snapshot.ts playGear case always uses 'equipped').
findings.reason: snapshot.ts:67-73 playGear case: with no targetUnitId, it returns `${actor} equipped ${card}.` unconditionally — no branch for non-equipment gear. Petricite Monument (cards/sfd/petricite-monument.ts:6) is cardType "gear" (not equipment), so playing it to base logs "dev equipped Petricite Monument." instead of "played".

findings.what: Empowered Ambessa in base (not in combat) is still dealt spell damage.
findings.expected: Per rulesText "[Empowered] > I have +3 Might and can't be dealt damage unless I'm in combat": Falling Star (Deal 3 + Deal 3) targeting Empowered Ambessa sitting in base should deal 0 damage.
findings.observed: After resolving Falling Star with both targets = Ambessa, her meta showed damage: 6 (__counters.damage 6, lastDamageSource 'spell') while empowered: true and located in base with no combat/showdown. Engine damage-immunity (operations/damage-immunity.ts) only supports a 'moved-this-turn' condition; no 'empowered && not in combat' restriction is registered for this card (ven.json parseSuccess:false, abilities:[]).
findings.reason: ven-084-166 exists only in packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ven.json with abilities:[] and parseSuccess:false (no TS override anywhere in packages/ or apps/). unitIgnoresDamage (damage-immunity.ts:36-52) iterates registry abilities looking for static restriction 'no-damage'; with an empty ability list it returns false, and conditionHolds (lines 21-34) only recognizes 'moved-this-turn' — there is no empowered/not-in-combat condition. So damage.ts applies Falling Star's damage to Empowered Ambessa in base.

findings.what: Sandbox/debug `stunUnit` move does not produce a stun that Solari Shrine's trigger recognizes (only writes meta.__flags.stunned, not top-level meta.stunned that the die-event snapshot reads).
findings.expected: An enemy unit that the state snapshot reports as stunned:true (stunned via the sandbox stunUnit action) and is then killed by my spell should fire 'When you kill a stunned enemy unit' exactly like a unit stunned by Rune Prison/Facebreaker does.
findings.observed: Enemy Recruit stunned via stunUnit (snapshot meta.stunned=true), Shrine ready, killed by Hextech Ray / Dancing Grenade / Super Mega Death Rocket cast by player-1 -> no chain item, no opt-in prompt, no draw (3 separate attempts, base and battlefield). Same kills on units stunned by a real stun spell (Rune Prison, Facebreaker) triggered correctly. abilities/effects/stun.ts mirrors the flag to meta.stunned; game-definition/moves/counters.ts stunUnit only calls counters.setFlag.
findings.reason: game-definition/moves/counters.ts:162-166 stunUnit only calls counters.setFlag(cardId,"stunned",true) (writes meta.__flags.stunned). Die-event emitters read top-level meta.stunned: cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:596 `wasStunned: unitMeta?.stunned === true` (damage-death path used by Hextech Ray etc.) and abilities/effects/kill.ts:193 `meta?.stunned === true`. trigger-matcher.ts:420 rejects the 'stunned' filter when event.wasStunned !== true. Real stun effect (abilities/effects/stun.ts:16-24) mirrors to top-level meta.stunned via updateCardMeta, which is why Rune Prison works. Snapshot (apps/riftbound-app/server/snapshot.ts:377) reads __flags.stunned first, so it shows stunned=true despite triggers not seeing it.

findings.what: Deflect surcharge is not paid when an opponent chooses Galio from a multi-candidate target prompt of a triggered ability.
findings.expected: Per Deflect ('Opponents must pay [rainbow] to choose me with a spell or ability'), when player-2's Blastcone Fae / Gem Jammer 'When you play me, ... a unit' ability picks Galio, player-2 should lose 1 power of any domain (as happens for spells: Vengeance->Galio correctly charged order2 + 1 extra fury).
findings.observed: Player-2 pool before pick {mind:0,fury:1}; resolvePendingChoice pickedCardId=Galio succeeded, effect applied to Galio (mightModifier -2 from Blastcone Fae; Ganking granted by Gem Jammer), pool after pick still {mind:0,fury:1} both times. Affordability gating does work (with 0 power Galio was excluded from Solari Shieldbearer's options), but pending-choice.ts never calls payAnyDomainPower/getDeflectSurcharge — only the auto-bound single-candidate branch in chain/resolve.ts charges.
findings.reason: chain/resolve.ts:453-466 filters options by Deflect affordability and at :517-530 sets a choose-target pendingChoice for >=2 options WITHOUT paying; only the single-candidate else-branch at :531-539 calls payAnyDomainPower(getDeflectSurcharge(...)). The comment at resolve.ts:450-452 claims the multi-candidate pick "still owes its surcharge at pick time (choose-target branch of pending-choice.ts)", but game-definition/moves/pending-choice.ts:1236-1267 (the plain choose-target resolution) just builds effectCtx with boundTargets=[picked] and calls executeEffect — no getDeflectSurcharge/payAnyDomainPower anywhere in pending-choice.ts (grep confirms zero references). So a prompted triggered-ability pick of Galio applies the effect without deducting power.

findings.what: Predict 2 offers no way to reorder the kept cards ('put the rest back in any order')
findings.expected: After looking at the top two cards and choosing which (if any) to recycle, the player should be able to choose the order of the remaining cards on top of the Main Deck (rulesText: 'Recycle any of them and put the rest back in any order').
findings.observed: Predict is implemented as sequential optional reveal-and-pick(recycle) prompts; choosing 'No' on the first prompt immediately ends the Predict with pendingChoice=null and the two cards left in their original order (Flame Chompers, Dangerous Duo) — no reorder prompt/move is ever offered. predict.ts comment confirms: 'recycle the pick, leave the rest on top … declining ends the Predict'.
findings.reason: predict.ts:35-45 builds Predict N as an optional reveal-and-pick with onPicked:"recycle" and a chained `then: {type:"predict", amount: remaining}` only; no reorder step exists. pending-choice.ts:1462-1480 handles the decline (accept===false): it clears draft.pendingChoice and returns without executing choice.then and without moving/reordering the revealed cards, so declining the first prompt ends the Predict with the cards in original order. No reorder move exists anywhere in game-definition/, server.ts, or the gameplay UI (grep for reorder/orderTop finds nothing; keyword-effects.ts:126 only describes "reorder rest" in text). Card text (dramatic-visionary.ts:14) says "put the rest back in any order".

findings.what: Unchosen cards from Lightning Rush's look-at-top-3 are recycled to the bottom of the Main Deck instead of put into the trash
findings.expected: rulesText: 'Put the rest into your trash.' After drawing 1 of the 3 revealed cards, the other 2 should be in player-1's trash (trash count +2, deck -3).
findings.observed: pendingChoice was {type:'reveal-and-pick', onPicked:'draw', onRest:'recycle'}; after picking Gust, trash count stayed at 1 (only Lightning Rush itself), deck went 35->34, and server state showed the two unpicked cards (player-1-main-14-unl-127-219, player-1-main-35-sfd-005-221) at mainDeck indices 68/69 (bottom). Reproduced again on the Flow replay (unpicked cards at mainDeck 65/66 of 67, trash 0). The spell ability loaded for the card is just {type:'look', amount:3, from:'deck'} with no rest->trash destination (ven.json abilities entry is [null]).
findings.reason: Parser drops the "Put the rest into your trash." clause: packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-draw.ts:139 returns bare `{ amount, from, type: "look" }` for Lightning Rush (ven.json:4460 abilities is [null], so runtime parse is used). The engine then defaults the rest-destination to recycle: packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/look.ts:53 `onRest = lookEff.onRest ?? (visionLike ? undefined : "recycle")`, and the only supported onRest value is "recycle" (look.ts:40, types/game-state.ts:522). pending-choice.ts:1466-1472/1793 moves the unpicked revealed cards to mainDeck position "bottom". No trash destination exists for look-rest, so the 2 unchosen cards go to deck bottom instead of trash, matching the observation.

findings.what: No way to decline the optional pick ('You may choose a card')
findings.expected: rulesText says 'You MAY choose a card from among them and draw it' — player should be able to choose none (all 3 then go to trash).
findings.observed: Only three resolvePendingChoice moves (one per revealed card) were offered; UI modal 'Choose a card to draw — Play is paused until you choose' had no skip button; executeMove('resolvePendingChoice',{playerId}) without pickedCardId was rejected ('condition not met').
findings.reason: ven-156-166 is a JSON-set card whose ability comes from the parser. parseLookEffect (packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-draw.ts:90-139) only special-cases the "You may banish ... and play it" tail; "You may choose a card from among them and draw it. Put the rest into your trash." falls through to line 139 `return { amount, from, type: "look" }` with no `optional: true` (verified by dumping getAllCards(): effect is exactly {amount:3,from:"deck",type:"look"}). handle_look (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/look.ts:97) only sets pendingChoice.optional when `visionLike || lookEff.optional`, so the reveal-and-pick choice is non-optional (and onRest defaults to "recycle", not trash, line 53). resolvePendingChoice then rejects accept:false unless choice.optional (game-definition/moves/pending-choice.ts:662) and the enumerator only pushes the {accept:false} decline variant when choice.optional (pending-choice.ts:803-804). Hence only the 3 pickedCardId moves are offered and a param-less/decline call fails 'condition not met'.

findings.what: Main spell instruction (choose two friendly units at different locations; if at least one has [Temporary], swap their locations) is entirely missing
findings.expected: On play, a prompt to choose a unit I control and another unit I control at a different location; with Keeper of Masks ([Temporary]) in base and a Sprite token at the battlefield, the two should have swapped locations on resolution, then Draw 1
findings.observed: No pendingChoice / no target params on playSpell; chain item effect was only {"amount":1,"type":"draw"}; after resolution Keeper of Masks stayed in base and Sprite stayed at battlefield-player-1-bf-ogn-276-298; only the draw happened. Built card abilities (getAllCards) confirm: [keyword Hidden, spell{draw 1}] — the choose/move clause is dropped at card/parser level
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/smoke-and-mirrors.ts:4-16 has no explicit `abilities` field; abilities are derived from rulesText via parseAbilities. Running parseAbilities on the card's rulesText yields exactly [{keyword Hidden}, {type:spell, timing:action, effect:{type:draw, amount:1}}] — the "Choose a unit you control and another unit you control at a different location. If at least one of them has [Temporary], move each to the other's location." clause is silently dropped at the parser layer, so no targeting/choice or swap effect exists for the engine to execute. Matches observed behavior (only draw 1 resolves).

findings.what: Deathknell does not fire when Tasty Faefolk dies from lethal damage applied via the sandbox `addDamage` move (Actions > Add Counters path).
findings.expected: Unit takes 6 damage, is killed by state-based cleanup, and its Deathknell (channel 2 runes exhausted + draw 1) goes on the chain — same as when it is killed by a spell.
findings.observed: executeMove('addDamage',{cardId:Faefolk,amount:6}) moved the unit to trash (base [], trash 1) but no chain item / pendingChoice appeared; runePool stayed at 2 runes and hand stayed at 5. The addDamage reducer calls performCleanup() directly (reaps without emitting `die` events), so the withPostMoveCleanup/cleanupAndFireDeaths pass finds nothing left to fire. Killing the same unit with Vengeance (kill effect) DID fire Deathknell correctly, so this is specific to the damage→SBA-death path used by the sandbox move.
findings.reason: counters.ts:62-81 — the `addDamage` reducer calls `performCleanup(...)` directly and discards its `CleanupResult`. `performCleanup` (cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:583-617) moves the lethal unit to trash, clears its damage, and only *returns* `deaths`/`killed`; it never dispatches `die` events itself — that is done by the caller in `runStateMaintenance` (events/dispatcher.ts:175-190 → `dispatchUnitDied`). `counterMoves` is not wrapped in `withPostMoveCleanup` (only movement.ts:24 is), and even if a later `cleanupAndFireDeaths` ran it would find nothing (damage already cleared, unit already in trash). Reproduced with the harness: `scenario().unit(P1,"base","ogn-075-298","fae")` then `p1.do("addDamage",{cardId:"fae",amount:6})` → zone=trash, chain=[], no pendingChoice; the same unit killed by a 6-damage spell puts `{cardId:"fae",triggered:true,type:"ability"}` on the chain.

findings.what: The 2 XP payment is neither required nor charged — the 'choose a card from their hand → they discard it' effect happens for free.
findings.expected: 'You may pay 2 XP to choose a card from their hand. If you do, they discard that card…' — with 0 XP the player must not be able to choose/discard; with ≥2 XP, choosing must deduct 2 XP.
findings.observed: Game A: player-1 XP=0, played Investigator, opt-in prompt 'Use Insightful Investigator ability? Yes/No' offered accept:true; accepting opened a reveal-and-pick over player-2's 4 cards, picking Cleave sent it to trash. XP stayed 0. Game B: gainXp 3 → played → accepted → picked Doran's Ring → discarded; player-1 XP stayed 3 (not reduced to 1). Engine's canPayOptInCost() only checks energy/power/exhaust, and nothing spends xp for a pay-cost {xp:2} on the opt-in path.
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/insightful-investigator.ts:24-43 places `{type:"pay-cost", cost:{xp:2}}` on the EFFECT's `conditional.condition`, not on the ability's `condition` (the file's own FIXME at lines 18-21 acknowledges the gating is wrong). Engine consequences: (1) trigger-runner.ts:1209 `extractPayCost(match.ability.condition)` returns undefined, so the chain item carries no `optInCost`; the opt-in prompt is offered purely because `optional: true` (trigger-runner.ts:1223) with no payability gate. (2) On accept, pending-choice.ts:948-956 finds no cost so nothing is deducted, then executeResolvedItem runs the `conditional` effect; abilities/effects/conditional.ts:14 calls `evaluateEffectCondition`, which has no `"pay-cost"` case (_helpers.ts:343-571) and falls to `default: return true` (_helpers.ts:568-570) — the reveal-hand/discard/draw `then` branch runs for free. (3) Even if optInCost were populated, `canPayOptInCost` (pending-choice.ts:279-308) checks only energy/power/exhaust and `deductAbilityCost` (activate-ability.ts:326+) never touches player.xp. Matches observed: XP=0 can accept and discard; XP=3 stays 3.

findings.what: Wrong player draws: the controller draws 1 instead of the opponent who discarded.
findings.expected: 'If you do, they discard that card and draw 1' — the chosen opponent (player-2) discards the picked card and then player-2 draws 1 (hand size stays 4, p2 deck −1). Player-1 draws nothing.
findings.observed: In both games player-1's hand grew by 1 (Sinister Poro / Chemtech Enforcer drawn; p1 main deck 35→34) and the draw happened immediately on accepting the opt-in, before any card was picked. Player-2 went 4→3 cards in hand and p2 main deck stayed at 36 (no draw). Card def models the follow-up as a bare {type:'draw',amount:1} in the controller's sequence.
findings.reason: insightful-investigator.ts:34 models the follow-up as `{ amount: 1, type: "draw" }` with no `player` field inside the controller's sequence. effects/draw.ts:33-82 (handle_draw) defaults to `ctx.playerId` (the controller) when `player` is neither "each" nor "target-controller", so player-1 draws instead of the opponent. The draw is also a sibling of the `reveal-hand` pending choice in the sequence (lines 28-36), so it executes immediately on opt-in rather than after the pick/discard, matching the observed timing. Rules text says "they discard that card and draw 1" — the opponent should draw.

findings.what: Hand reveal is gated behind the optional payment/opt-in instead of being unconditional.
findings.expected: 'When you play me, choose an opponent. They reveal their hand.' happens always; only the choose-and-discard part is optional (pay 2 XP). Declining to pay should still reveal the opponent's hand.
findings.observed: Game C: played Investigator, answered 'No' to the opt-in prompt → trigger ended with no reveal step at all (no reveal/reveal-and-pick pendingChoice, no log entry, state unchanged). The reveal only occurs inside the accepted branch (card def wraps reveal-hand inside the pay-cost conditional; def carries a FIXME acknowledging this).
findings.reason: insightful-investigator.ts:24-43 — the triggered ability is `optional: true` (line 40) and its sole effect is a `conditional` with `condition: {type:"pay-cost", cost:{xp:2}}` (line 26) whose `then` sequence contains the `reveal-hand` effect (lines 29-33) plus draw. There is no unconditional reveal-hand outside the pay-cost branch and no `else`, so declining the opt-in/payment skips the reveal entirely. The FIXME at lines 18-21 explicitly states the entire reveal-hand+draw sequence was gated behind the XP cost. Rules text (line 57) says reveal is unconditional; only the pick/discard/draw is 'You may pay 2 XP'.

findings.what: Opt-in prompt does not state the cost and the pick modal has no way to decline after seeing the hand.

Otherwise, counter it."}` — the "Choose a spell with Energy cost no more than 4" clause produces no target descriptor and no counter/gain-control-of-spell effect type. Consequently:
- /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/targeting.ts:343-436 `spellEffectHasLegalTargets` — the `raw` effect matches none of the counter (line 402) / gain-control-of-spell (line 409) chain-gates and has no target/target1/etc., so it falls through to `return true` at line 436.

findings.what: Sprite token created by Trevor's hold trigger is displayed with Might 1 instead of 3
findings.expected: rulesText says 'play a ready 3 [Might] Sprite unit token' -> token should show Might 3 in game state/UI
findings.observed: State snapshot (/api/game/:id/state and pw state bfZones) reports the token as {name:'Sprite', might:1, definitionId:'token-def-sprite'}. Engine internally treats it as Might 3 (addDamage 2 -> survived with damage 2; addDamage +1 (total 3) -> killed), so the snapshot builder is resolving might from the shared per-name 'token-def-sprite' definition (catalog Sprite = 1 Might/Backline) rather than the per-instance registration that carries might 3 + Temporary.
findings.reason: snapshot.ts:366-368,397 resolves `might` from `cardInstance.definitionId`, which effect-context.ts:85-89 stamps as the shared `token-def-sprite` for every ability-minted Sprite. That shared id is registered first-writer-wins in the process-global registry: token.ts:70-75 (RIFTBOUND_TOKEN_DEFS.Sprite = might 1, Backline) via addToken at token.ts:131-143, and create-token.ts:119 skips re-registering if it already exists (`if (!registry.get(tokenDefinitionId))`). Meanwhile create-token.ts:199-207 registers the per-instance id with tokenDef.might=3, which is what damage/kill logic reads. So once the catalog Sprite (might 1) has been registered in the server process (sandbox addToken / earlier game), Trevor's 3-Might Temporary Sprite is displayed as might 1 in /api/game/:id/state while the engine treats it as 3 — exactly the observed divergence. findings.what: Shadow Watcher's conditional 'I enter ready' is applied unconditionally
findings.expected: On turn 1 with no friendly unit having died during my Beginning Phase, Shadow Watcher should enter exhausted (rule 143.4 default) because the condition 'If a friendly unit died during your Beginning Phase this turn' is false.
findings.observed: Fresh game, turn 1 main phase, empty board, no deaths at all this game: played Shadow Watcher to base and it entered READY (state exhausted=false, card upright in screenshot). Root cause from code: parser emits condition {type:'custom', text:'If a friendly unit died during your Beginning Phase this turn'} for this text; evaluateEnterReadyCondition (moves/play/cost.ts) hits the default branch and returns undefined, and staticEnterReadyApplies treats `!== false` as satisfied, so any unrecognized enter-ready condition grants ready. There is also no engine tracking of 'friendly unit died during Beginning Phase' (state.turnEvents not populated for this).
findings.reason: Reproduced with harness: scenario with 4 energy + 1 calm, no units/deaths, play unl-037-219 to base -> state isReady=true, isExhausted=false (expected exhausted per rule 143.4). Parser output for the rules text is {type:'static', effect:{type:'enter-ready'}, condition:{type:'custom', text:'If a friendly unit died during your Beginning Phase this turn'}}. In cost.ts, evaluateEnterReadyCondition has no 'custom' case and hits `default: return undefined` (lines 265-267); staticEnterReadyApplies at line 96 uses `evaluateEnterReadyCondition(...) !== false` so undefined is treated as satisfied and returns true. No engine tracking exists for 'friendly unit died during Beginning Phase' (turnEvents undefined in repro).

findings.what: Mode 1 'Choose up to 3 cards from opponents' trashes. Their owners recycle them.' recycles the CASTER's own trash instead of opponents' and gives no target prompt.
findings.expected: After picking the recycle mode, a prompt to choose up to 3 (optionally 0) cards from player-2's trash (which held 4 cards); chosen cards go to the bottom of player-2's main deck; player-1's trash untouched.
findings.observed: No prompt appeared. Player-2's trash stayed at 4 cards / deck 33. Instead every card in player-1's trash (first run: the just-resolved Disposal Order itself, p1 deck 33->34; second run: two Disposal Orders, p1 trash 2->0, deck 32->34) was auto-recycled to the bottom of player-1's deck. Root cause in engine handle_recycle (abilities/effects/recycle.ts): the counted 'from: trash' branch pools only ctx.playerId's trash unless effect.owner==='any' and reads effect.upTo, ignoring the card's target {controller:'enemy', location:'trash', quantity:{upTo:3}} — so the enemy filter and the up-to/optional prompt are both dropped.
findings.reason: Card def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/disposal-order.ts:24-34) emits {type:'recycle', amount:3, from:'trash', target:{controller:'enemy', location:'trash', quantity:{upTo:3}, type:'card'}} with no `owner` or top-level `upTo`. In handle_recycle (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/recycle.ts:129-166) the counted `from:'trash'` branch builds `owners = effect.owner==='any' ? allPlayers : [ctx.playerId]` (lines 134-137) and pools only those trashes (138-140) — never consulting effect.target.controller, so it pools the CASTER's trash. `upTo` is read from `effect.upTo === true` (line 145), not target.quantity.upTo, so upTo=false; with n = min(3, pool.length) == pool.length the prompt branch (149) is skipped and lines 162-165 auto-recycle every card in the caster's trash. Matches observed: no prompt, p1's own trash (1 or 2 Disposal Orders) recycled to p1 deck, p2 trash untouched.

findings.expected: With fury power available, pw moves should list a paidAdditionalCost playUnit variant (as it does for e.g. Gust Monk ven-101-166), paying it should spend 1 fury and set paidAdditionalCost=true so the play trigger readies Pyke and gives +2 Might this turn

findings.reason: Pyke's hand-authored card def (packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/pyke-dockside-butcher.ts:14-34) declares only Hidden, Ganking, and the paid-additional-cost triggered ability; because `abilities` is explicitly set, enrichCard skips rulesText parsing (data/enrich-cards.ts:23), so no `{type:"static", effect:{type:"additional-cost-option", additionalCost}}` ability exists. getOptionalPlayCost (riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/cost.ts:909-1024) only returns a cost for Accelerate / kill / static additional-cost-option shapes, so it returns undefined for unl-028-219 and resolvePayableOptionalCost (play-unit.ts:71-79) never yields a paid variant. Verified at runtime via getAllCards(): Pyke's loaded abilities have no additional-cost-option entry, whereas Gust Monk ven-101-166 (parsed from rulesText) has `{type:"static", effect:{type:"additional-cost-option", additionalCost:":rb_energy_1:", optional:true}}`.

findings.what: Optional additional cost "kill a friendly gear" is never offered/payable when playing Zaun Punk
findings.expected: With 2 friendly gears (Orb of Regret, Mask of Foresight) on base and enough energy, move enumeration should offer paid playUnit variants (paidAdditionalCost:true + sacrificeId per gear), and paying it should kill the chosen gear (rule 356/560).
findings.observed: Server /moves and UI listed only the plain playUnit {cardId,location:base,playerId} for Zaun Punk — no sacrifice variants. Forcing executeMove('playUnit',{...,paidAdditionalCost:true,sacrificeId:<Orb of Regret>}) played the unit (energy 15->12, Zaun Punk on base) but the named gear stayed on base and trash stayed 0. Root cause: card's parsed abilities contain only the triggered payoff; the 'You may kill a friendly gear as an additional cost to play me' clause produced no static/additional-cost-option ability with cost.kill, so getOptionalPlayCost() returns undefined.
findings.reason: zaun-punk.ts:4-16 defines no `abilities`, so enrichCards re-parses rulesText. Running parseAbilities on the card text (verified via bun) yields only the triggered payoff `{type:"triggered", trigger:{event:"play-self"}, condition:{type:"paid-additional-cost"}, effect:{type:"kill",target:{type:"gear"}}}` — the "You may kill a friendly gear as an additional cost to play me" clause is dropped: parser/impl/replacement.ts:38-54 only matches "You may pay COST"/"spend N XP" variants and parser/impl/spells.ts:135 handles the spell-only mandatory form; no unit "you may kill a friendly X" pattern exists. Consequently getOptionalPlayCost (riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/cost.ts:909-930) finds no static/additional-cost-option ability with cost.kill and returns undefined (verified: prints `undefined` for sfd-160-221 with real registry), so play-unit.ts enumerator emits no sacrifice variants and the reducer at play-unit.ts:996 (`optional = paidAdditionalCost ? getOptionalPlayCost(cardId) : undefined`) never kills the gear. Engine path itself works when the ability shape is present (rules-audit/optional-play-cost.test.ts:209-257 uses a hand-crafted `{type:"static", cost:{kill:{controller:"friendly",type:"gear"}}}`), confirming this is a card/parser-layer gap.

findings.what: "When you play me, if you paid the additional cost, kill a gear" payoff can never fire
findings.expected: After paying the kill-gear additional cost, a play-self trigger should go on the chain prompting to kill a gear (the remaining Mask of Foresight).
findings.observed: No chain item / pendingChoice after play; both gears remained. Unreachable because the additional cost cannot be paid (see bug 1).
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/zaun-punk.ts:4-16 has no hand-authored `abilities`, so enrich-cards.ts:29 runs parseAbilities on the rulesText. Verified by running the parser/getAllCards(): the enriched sfd-160-221 carries ONLY `{type:"triggered", trigger:{event:"play-self"}, condition:{type:"paid-additional-cost"}, effect:{type:"kill", target:{type:"gear"}}}` — the sentence "You may kill a friendly gear as an additional cost to play me." fails to parse (parseAbilities returns success:false for it alone) and yields no additional-cost ability. Consequently getOptionalPlayCost (riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/cost.ts:909-1024) returns undefined for this card, playUnit's enumerator never emits a paidAdditionalCost/sacrificeId variant, the reducer fires play-self with paidAdditionalCost=false (play-unit.ts:1110, 1207), and trigger-runner.ts:289-293 gates the payoff on event.paidAdditionalCost===true, so the kill-a-gear trigger can never go on the chain. Engine plumbing works when the cost ability exists (rules-audit/optional-play-cost.test.ts:209 hand-authors `{type:"static", cost:{kill:{controller:"friendly",type:"gear"}}}`), confirming this is a card-layer gap: the payoff is unreachable because the real card lacks the additional-cost ability.

findings.what: Trusty Ramhound gets +1 Might even when it is the only unit at its location
findings.expected: Alone at base: Might 2 (printed). Only +1 while another friendly unit is at the same location.
findings.observed: Fresh game, played Ramhound to an empty base: server state meta.staticMightBonus=1 and the board might badge (.card-might) shows 3 with no other unit at base. Cause: parser emits condition {type:'custom', text:'While you have another unit here'} and static-abilities.ts default branch treats unknown conditions as true, so the bonus is unconditional.
findings.reason: Card def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/trusty-ramhound.ts) has no explicit abilities, so enrich-cards.ts:30 runs parseAbilities on rulesText. Verified by running the parser: output is {condition:{type:"custom",text:"While you have another unit here"}, effect:{type:"modify-might",amount:1,target:"self"}} — produced by static-parser.ts:658-665 (whileConditionMightMatch fallback to type "custom" when parseConditionFromText fails). In the engine, static-abilities.ts:749 calls evaluateCondition; the switch at static-abilities.ts:112 has no "custom" case, so it hits the default at static-abilities.ts:330-333 which returns true. The +1 Might is therefore applied unconditionally, including when Ramhound is alone.
